# XER Schedule Check: DCMA 14-point assessment of a Primavera P6 XER file

> Free, in-browser DCMA 14-point schedule check for Primavera P6 .xer exports. It reads the XER tables, recomputes early and late dates and total float on each activity's own calendar with P6's relationship, lag-calendar, constraint and progress rules (equal to P6's stored values on 19,732 of 19,822 open activities, 99.5%, in six public files from P6 5.0 to 24.12), runs the 14 points with the DCMA thresholds and a 600-day critical path test, and lists every activity behind each finding, plus logic loops, out-of-sequence progress and open finishes. It also compares two monthly updates of one project: progress claimed, actual dates edited after reporting, logic, duration, constraint and calendar changes, float used, driving-path changes, and a half-step run that splits the finish movement into progress and revisions. Nothing is uploaded.

Free and open source (MIT). Screening metrics on the user's own file, not scheduling, contractual or legal advice. Missed tasks and BEI use P6's planned dates as the baseline because a single XER rarely carries the baseline project. Not modelled: resource levelling, expected finish dates, multiple float paths. Not affiliated with Oracle, Primavera or the DCMA.

## Pages

- [The tool](https://marisstella.app/xer-schedule-check/)

## For agents

- Engine: `xer.mjs` `parseXer(decodeXer(bytes))`; `cpm.mjs` `schedule(xer)` (dates in wall-clock minutes, float in hours) and `drivingPath(result, projId)`; `dcma.mjs` `assess(xer, { projId })` returns `{ project, checks[14], extra, recompute, drivingPath }` and `findingsCsv(report)`.
- `compare.mjs` `compare(prevXer, curXer)` returns `{ previous, current, finish: { moved, halfStep, progressEffect, revisionEffect }, flags, progress, logic, durations, constraints, calendars, activities, float, criticalPath }`; `compareCsv(rep)`, `compareText(rep)`.
- CLI: `node cli.mjs schedule.xer [--json] [--csv out.csv] [--project CODE]`; `node cli.mjs current.xer --previous previous.xer [--json] [--csv changes.csv] [--project CODE]` (the previous file's project is matched by project ID; CSV cells that would run as spreadsheet formulas are written as text).
